conbody.p: Impact, under Verify in the project menu, answers "what does a change to this requirement touch?" before you make it. Pick the requirement, or open the page from Show impact → on a requirement or a row of the Traceability Matrix. Only requirements can be picked: the analysis always starts from one, and flows from it to every artifact its links lead to.

ul.li: The result is a tree with the requirement in the middle. Upstream — what it depends on, its sources and rationale — branches out to the left; Downstream — what depends on it, what a change here could affect — branches out to the right. Each artifact hangs off the one it was reached through.

Each line, and the edge of the box it leads to, is coloured by its link type, with a key below the tree, so a satisfies reads apart from a verifies or a mitigates at a glance. Select a box to open the artifact.
Depth — 1 level shows only the artifacts linked directly to the requirement; All levels follows every link to the end of the chain.

The walk follows every link, hop after hop. Downstream it reaches the sub-requirements, the design items that satisfy them, the test cases that verify them and the hazards those design items mitigate; upstream it reaches the user needs and parent requirements. An impacts link counts as the change flowing from its source to its target, and a relates-to link, having no direction, is followed both ways.
On a phone the tree opens on the requirement; swipe sideways to follow it.

conbody.p: Run it before changing an approved requirement: the downstream list is the set of artifacts whose links will turn suspect and that may need review again.
